rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm this rule guards: a cross-module claim that drifts from what the referenced module actually teaches sends a trainer or student into that module with the wrong mental model, and per the rule's own text this class of error is 'the most expensive to catch late.' Harm is present, not theoretical. Line 282: '**AE101 cross-refs:** ... M6 hands you a handoff prompt that authors more, one per recurring shape in your stack.' Line 347 (softer echo): 'The skills your M6 handoff prompt authors are strong candidates to wire into a schedule like this one.' Both describe the WIDENED M6 handoff design. The actual M6 handoff prompt — curriculum/prompts/agents-that-build-agents-handoff.md, rewritten in commit 95d2b003 ('The handoff prompt builds one skill and its checks, not the kit', 2026-09-03T20:00) — now asks for exactly ONE skill, picked together with the agent, plus checks on its output; its own maintainer note in curriculum/lectures/the-handoff-prompt.md states the narrowing explicitly: 'one skill, not the kit, Antti 2026-09-03: a cold session asked for N skills from two starting points does not finish inside a three-minute beat; do not re-widen.' This reference page's M6 cross-ref was itself last synced to M6 in commit 4e0370bc (2026-09-02T21:14, 'The pages that describe M6 catch up with the M6 that exists') — 23 hours BEFORE the handoff prompt's own narrowing landed, so the sync commit is honest for its moment and stale now. Corroborating: the same stale 'authors further skills' claim also survives in curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/earn-the-trust.md line 185 (a different file, out of this judge's scope, but confirming the drift is real and not a misreading of this file alone). All other §4 facets on this file are clean: no front-run of a downstream teaching moment (the page is a flat primitive lookup, not a narrative), no Big-Idea framing to honor (N/A per check_strategy_tie_in §3, already parked), no mood-arc to preempt (mood-floor exempt per this file's own parked §1/§2 rows).
